body:
I confirm that this is used downstream for some thirdparty platforms.

So we should document that so that it doesn't appear as dead code, or see if there's an easy way for thirdparty platforms to keep such code downstream instead of in FileAccessMemory. FileAccessMemory seems to have fairly limited usage in the upstream repo from what I can see (used in some texture and scene format importers, and editor translations).

CC @Eoin-ONeill-Yokai

This is useful for many situations, the most popular is probably when a game downloads a file from the network and needs to hand it over to a `ResourceLoader` without writing it to disk. Another common use is, when a game is small enough, load the whole PCK in memory, then do all file operations on that memory buffer instead of doing disk i/o (consoles benefit from this especially). The `FileAccessBuffered` had similar utility.

The FileAccessMemory itself is limited in 2 ways in my experience:
- There's no way to access `FileAccessMemory::register_file` from gdscript, this would allow a game to download a file to memory and register it as a path from gdscript, so that other systems can open it
- There's no way to open the files registered in `FileAccessMemory::register_file`, other than using the `FileAccessMemory` interface. This could be solved by adding a check in `FileAccess::open` to see if `FileAccessMemory` has the path, similar to what we do for `PackedData`

Usually projects that use this feature implement those internally, it's a handful of lines of code for each.

The way to properly get rid of this in my opinion would be to add some mechanism to register paths or schemes to be handled by a custom FileAccess implementation, then make `FileAccess::open` use the proper one, probably selected in `FileAccess::create_for_path`. The PCK handler could go there, as well as the different implementations of `FileAccess` for `res://` or `user://`, etc. Then, if a 3rd party module wants to use memory, they can add their handler there and implement their own `FileAccessMemory` that should properly interact with the `ResourceLoader` without having to do core changes.

> The way to properly get rid of this in my opinion would be to add some mechanism to register paths or schemes to be handled by a custom FileAccess implementation

There's a proposal for this: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6307

And a couple attempts at implementation:

- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/87586
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/98544
